text.title: Micro-MVPs Procedure
text.summary: Step-by-step procedure to apply Micro-MVPs end-to-end. Each step names its input, action, and output.

step.name: decide
step.action: Hit success → continue / scale; hit kill → archive.

section.title: Experiment design loop
section.p: Six-step process for designing, running, and acting on a micro-MVP experiment. It runs inside steps 1–4 above at finer grain: steps 1–3 here refine scope and thresholds, 4–5 refine ship and decide, 6 chooses the next cycle.

step.name: riskiest-assumption
step.action: Step 1: Identify the riskiest assumption — the one belief, if wrong, that kills the product idea entirely.
step.note: Testing a secondary assumption first wastes time. Riskiest assumption first forces prioritisation by existential risk, not build convenience.

step.name: smallest-experiment
step.action: Step 2: Design the smallest experiment that can falsify or confirm that single assumption. One assumption per experiment.
step.note: Multi-assumption experiments produce ambiguous results. If the experiment fails, you do not know which assumption was wrong.

step.name: pre-commit-metrics
step.action: Step 3: Define success metrics before starting, not after seeing results. Specify the threshold that means "confirmed" vs "rejected".
step.note: Defining metrics after seeing results produces motivated reasoning. Pre-commitment makes the experiment falsifiable.

step.name: run
step.action: Step 4: Run the experiment in hours to days. If it takes longer than one week, it is not a micro-MVP — split or simplify.
step.note: Speed is the whole point. A week-long micro-MVP competes with a two-week sprint and loses the argument for the lighter method.

step.name: analyse
step.action: Step 5: Analyse results against the pre-defined threshold. Binary outcome: confirmed or rejected.
step.note: Avoiding a clear verdict extends limbo. Even a failed experiment is valuable — it redirects effort before a full build.

step.name: next-move
step.action: Step 6: Decide: pivot (change the assumption and test again), persevere (move to building), or test the next riskiest assumption.
step.note: One confirmed micro-MVP is not enough to build. Stack experiments until the top 2–3 existential assumptions are validated before committing to a sprint.
